rules.title: NJ Security Deposit Law – cap and handling
rules.requirement: A landlord may not collect a security deposit above 1.5 times one month's rent, and yearly increases to the deposit may not exceed 10%. Prepaid rent such as last month's rent counts toward the cap, and deposits must be held in trust in an interest-bearing New Jersey account.
rules.quoted_span: The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ). It can be less.

unverifiable_exemptions: owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling (tenant may opt in by written request)

rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, unless the tenant sends a written request; interest rules do not apply to seasonal rentals.

rules.title: NJ Anti-Eviction Act – good cause required for non-renewal
rules.requirement: A landlord may not refuse to renew a lease, or evict a tenant just because the lease term ended, without good cause as defined in the Anti-Eviction Act. Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, motels/hotels and transient or seasonal units are not covered by this requirement.
rules.quoted_span: No landlord of residential rental properties except t hose in owner occupied two or three family dwellings, motels or hotels, transient, or seasonal units may fail to renew any lease
rules.key_value: good cause required for eviction or non-renewal

unverifiable_exemptions: motels or hotels, transient or seasonal units

rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, motels, hotels, transient or seasonal units.
rules.conflict_note: The guide cites the statute as 'N.J.S.A. 2A:18:61.3'. The citation is normalized to 2A:18-61.3.

parsed.doc_summary: Part 1 of the NJ DCA Truth in Renting guide. It states the NJ security deposit cap (1.5 months' rent, annual increase max 10%, handling rules) and the good-cause requirement for lease non-renewal under the Anti-Eviction Act. The rent control, screening fee and eviction-cause sections fall in later parts.
